plotEn:
In 1995, American literary editor Edward Ridgeway travels to Switzerland in the hopes of convincing author Patricia Highsmith to write a sixth book featuring her famed character Tom Ripley. His predecessor in the task, Bradley Appleby, has disappeared, believed by Edward’s bosses to be suffering a psychotic episode. While on the train to Tegna, he meets Clementine Balfour, a fellow American and wealthy young woman who is visiting family in Europe. During a taxi ride to Highsmith’s house, the driver unnerves him by telling stories of Highsmith allegedly killing a dog, and a man that may have been Appleby running down the road in pajamas in the middle of the night.
Upon his arrival, Edward meets Patricia, finding her eccentric, confrontational, and very opposed to writing another book about Tom Ripley, whom she says is ‘always in her company.’ Edward slowly earns her interest and respect, revealing his knowledge of her work, his lower-class upbringing, and that he is an orphan. He also delivers her supplies, including an ornate hunting knife for her extensive collection of weapons. She reluctantly agrees to allow him to stay for one night, and to assist her with plotting a new book, but refuses to sign a contract agreeing to write the book until she is satisfied with their work. Later that night, Edward awakes with blood on his neck, possibly from a cut made by a knife, which he suspects is from Patricia.
